title: Right to privacy as a fundamental right - the practical implications
p1: Your phone knows more about you than most people in your life. But does the law protect that information? The answer changed when the right to privacy was recognized as a fundamental right in India.
p2: Many people think privacy only means keeping personal conversations secret. The reality is much broader. Privacy also covers choices about your body, personal decisions, financial information, digital data, and how your identity is used. A surprising point: even everyday data collection by apps and companies can raise privacy concerns.
p3: This right does not mean the government or businesses can never access information. It means any interference must have a valid reason, follow legal safeguards, and respect individual freedom. For ordinary citizens, this translates into being more careful about app permissions, online sharing, and personal data. Privacy is not about hiding something; it is about having control over your own life.
conclusion: Do you think people today are giving away too much personal information without realizing the consequences?
